info.title: dssharness
info.description: Cross-platform repository harness CLI: git worktree management with Windows path-budget checks, driven entirely by .harness-config/config.json.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: DssHarness - cross-platform repository harness. Run 'dssharness help' for reference material.

commands.name: check-mutations
commands.description: Prove each selected leg's tests can fail: in worker copies of its tree, mutate each arm the registry declares, build it, witness every object depending on the site rebuilt, run its test binary whole, and judge what reddened against what the arm declares.

options.name: --legs
options.description: Only these legs or leg sets: --legs a,b or --legs a b. Without it, every declared leg.

options.name: --arms
options.description: Only these arms of the registry - with --self-test, of the fixture's - by id: --arms a,b or --arms a b. Without it, every arm.

options.name: --json
options.description: Write the per-leg ledger as JSON, each arm beneath its leg.

options.name: --force-lock
options.description: Take a lock, or a worker, another run holds, on this host or another. Always a human decision.

options.name: --use-staged
options.description: Sweep what is already staged on each copy, without syncing again. Legs on a copy a sync or a takeover began and did not finish, that is not there, or that holds no copy this tool made are inputs-moved.

options.name: --self-test
options.description: Sweep the fixture this tool carries instead of the registry's arms, built the way each selected leg builds, and hold each of its arms to the verdict it is designed to reach: proves this tool judges arms rightly with that leg's toolchain.

options.name: --list
options.description: Sweep nothing: say each selected arm's last verdict on each leg and whether anything it was judged on that this machine reads has moved since. Asks no host, takes no lock, begins no run and writes nothing; exits 0 whatever is pending.

options.name: --pending
options.description: Drive on each leg only the arms with no recorded passed that still holds: its first worker is made alone, each arm's key read from its build, and an arm whose key is a recorded passed's is left out, skipped-not-selected, saying which run's passed holds. With nothing pending the leg passes, and nothing is swept.

commands.name: create-agent
commands.description: Create an agent of an orchestrator: its record, its worktree, and its seed - the main tree's uncommitted state handed to it, each changed file copied and each deletion made, every path recorded; refused past the orchestrator's limit. With --no-worktree, the engine's agent: a record, with no worktree or seed, counted against no limit.

options.name: --model
options.description: The model the agent's session runs on, as its id.

options.name: --empty
options.description: Hand it nothing: record that it was made at a commit and given none of the main tree's uncommitted state.

options.name: --no-worktree
options.description: Used by the orchestrator engine for a step that only reads; of no use typed by hand. Makes an agent that has no worktree: it reads the main tree and keeps only records. Nothing of it is seeded, refreshed, rebased or folded.

options.name: --session
options.description: The agent's Claude session id, or its subagent's id, whose transcripts delete-agent keeps. Run again, it records only this. Not with --no-worktree: that agent records none.

commands.name: delete-agent
commands.description: Delete an agent: fold what is left of it and apply its rows, keep its evidence and transcripts, then remove its worktree and its copies on hosts; its directory stays as its history.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Do it; without it, only say what would be done, and exit as --apply would.

options.name: --merge
options.description: A path both trees changed whose three-way merge is clean, as the dry run says of it: the merged file is written into both trees and recorded as shared. Never taken unasked, and a clean textual merge proves nothing about the program. Once for each path.

options.name: --settled
options.description: A path you reconciled in the main tree by hand: the fold hands the agent the main tree's copy and records it as shared, so the rest can go in and its next fold starts from it. Refused where only the agent changed the path. Once for each path.

options.name: --new
options.description: The id of a row the agent filed that the fold may make: a row no registry holds is otherwise refused, as a typo in an existing row's id would make it a second row. Once for each id.

options.name: --accept-lost
options.description: A cell of an existing row - trigger, closing, cross-refs - the fold may write though the agent's text does not keep its stored text word for word: read its word diff in the dry run first. Once for each cell.

options.name: --accept-over
options.description: A cell of a row an earlier fold of the agent applied - priority, status, trigger, closing, cross-refs - that the registries and the agent both changed since, each otherwise: the fold may write the agent's over the registries'. Read the three texts in the dry run first. Once for each cell.

options.name: --discard-uncommitted
options.description: Abandon the agent: fold nothing and apply no rows, and remove its worktree with its changes; its evidence and transcripts are still kept.

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the outcome as one JSON document, the whole of standard output: its exit code, its summary and its lines, what is wanted of you before --apply would go through, and who holds what it needs.

commands.name: fix-line-endings
commands.description: Rewrite files to the line endings .gitattributes declares for them, read through 'git check-attr'. The policy is never restated here, so one statement of it governs both what git stores and what this writes. A file declared text=auto that git's own detection calls binary - a NUL anywhere, a carriage return no line feed follows, or more than one control byte for every 128 that print - is left as git leaves it; one declared text, or given an eol alone, is rewritten whatever it holds, as git converts it.

commands.name: fold-agent
commands.description: Fold a live agent's own changes into the main tree, then apply the anchor rows it filed: everything that refuses it is named before anything is written, a path both trees changed with what a three-way merge of it gives, which --merge takes where it is clean; the rows go in all or nothing, and a file of either tree that changed after it was weighed stops the fold part way (exit 21) rather than being written over or copied changed; its worktree is kept.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Write the fold and the rows; without it, only say what would be written, and exit as --apply would.

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the outcome as one JSON document, the whole of standard output: its exit code, its summary and its lines, what is wanted of you before --apply would go through, and who holds what it needs.

options.name: --merge
options.description: A path both trees changed whose three-way merge is clean, as the dry run says of it: the merged file is written into both trees and recorded as shared. Never taken unasked, and a clean textual merge proves nothing about the program. Once for each path.

options.name: --settled
options.description: A path you reconciled in the main tree by hand: the fold hands the agent the main tree's copy and records it as shared, so the rest can go in and its next fold starts from it. Refused where only the agent changed the path. Once for each path.

options.name: --new
options.description: The id of a row the agent filed that the fold may make: a row no registry holds is otherwise refused, as a typo in an existing row's id would make it a second row. Once for each id.

options.name: --accept-lost
options.description: A cell of an existing row - trigger, closing, cross-refs - the fold may write though the agent's text does not keep its stored text word for word: read its word diff in the dry run first. Once for each cell.

options.name: --accept-over
options.description: A cell of a row an earlier fold of the agent applied - priority, status, trigger, closing, cross-refs - that the registries and the agent both changed since, each otherwise: the fold may write the agent's over the registries'. Read the three texts in the dry run first. Once for each cell.
